blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Few HR practices have been as fiercely debated in the last decade as performance management. The traditional annual review — ratings, forced distributions, individual bonuses — has been criticised as demotivating, backward-looking and statistically unreliable. Several well-known companies have dismantled theirs, only to quietly reintroduce elements a few years later.

The underlying tension is honest. On one hand, organisations need differentiation: to reward contribution, make investment decisions and hold people accountable. On the other, most employees experience formal ratings as reductive and anxiety-inducing, particularly when they are tied to compensation.

The most thoughtful systems today are hybrid. They separate development conversations, which are frequent and genuinely forward-looking, from compensation decisions, which are deliberate and transparent but less central to daily life. They also invest heavily in manager capability, recognising that no system, however elegant, can compensate for a manager who avoids honest conversations.

items.q: According to the text, what happened after several companies dismantled their performance systems?
options: They quietly reintroduced elements a few years later
items.why: "Several well-known companies have dismantled theirs, only to quietly reintroduce elements a few years later."

items.q: What does the author call "the underlying tension"?
options: The conflict between HR and finance
The need for differentiation versus how employees experience ratings
The cost of running a rating system
The choice between annual and quarterly reviews
items.why: A tensão é entre a diferenciação de que a empresa precisa e a experiência redutora que os avaliados têm das notas.

items.q: How do hybrid systems treat development and compensation?
options: They merge both into a single annual event
They separate frequent, forward-looking development from deliberate compensation decisions
They rank employees before every pay review
items.why: "They separate development conversations… from compensation decisions."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Ratings can feel reductive when tied to pay
A well-designed system can rescue a manager who avoids hard conversations
The annual review is statistically unreliable
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma que nenhum sistema, por mais elegante, compensa um gestor que foge das conversas honestas.

items.q: The phrase "only to quietly reintroduce elements" suggests that the author believes…
options: annual reviews are the only workable option
abolishing appraisal entirely is harder than it looks
companies never learn from their mistakes
items.why: Inferência: o retorno silencioso dos elementos indica que abolir totalmente a avaliação não se sustenta na prática.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando o redesenho do sistema à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. Before I show you the new design, let me be candid about the constraint I've been working within. The board wants sharper differentiation — a way to see, clearly, who is driving the business. The workforce, meanwhile, is telling us in every survey that the ratings feel arbitrary and, frankly, demoralising. Both of those signals are legitimate, and I refuse to pretend one of them away.

So here is what I'm proposing. We split the two things we have wrongly bolted together. Development conversations become monthly, forward-looking and entirely separate from pay — no scores, just genuine coaching. Compensation, by contrast, is decided twice a year in a proper calibration session, transparent about the criteria and owned by leadership, not buried in a form.

But I want to be honest with you: the mechanism is the easy part. If our managers keep dodging the difficult conversation, no elegant framework will save us. That's why half of this budget goes into manager capability, not software. Rate the process all you like — what actually moves the needle is whether a manager can look someone in the eye and tell them the truth, kindly.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What are the two conflicting signals Sophie says she refuses to ignore?
options: The board's demand for differentiation and the workforce's dislike of the ratings
items.why: "The board wants sharper differentiation… The workforce… is telling us the ratings feel arbitrary."

items.q: How does Sophie propose to handle development conversations?
options: Only when a promotion is due
Monthly, forward-looking and separate from pay
items.why: "Development conversations become monthly, forward-looking and entirely separate from pay."

items.q: When and how are compensation decisions made under her proposal?
options: Twice a year, in a transparent calibration session owned by leadership
Once a year, hidden inside the appraisal form
items.why: "Compensation… is decided twice a year in a proper calibration session, transparent about the criteria."

items.q: What does Sophie mean when she says "the mechanism is the easy part"?
options: The software will handle most of the work
The board will approve it quickly
The real difficulty is getting managers to have honest conversations, not designing the process
The system can be built cheaply
items.why: Inferência: ela contrasta o desenho fácil com o desafio real — a capacidade dos gestores de conversar com franqueza.

items.q: What can be inferred about why half the budget goes to manager capability?
options: Software has become more expensive than training
Sophie believes the quality of the conversation matters more than the form of the system
The board mandated spending on coaching
items.why: Inferência: para Sophie, nenhum framework salva a empresa se o gestor foge da conversa — o investimento está na conversa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board pressed HR to overhaul its performance management." Performance management is…
options: the way an organisation sets, reviews and rewards how people work
items.why: Performance management = gestão de desempenho: como a empresa define, avalia e recompensa o trabalho.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Ranking a fixed percentage of staff as low performers every year is called a ___."
items.why: Forced distribution = distribuição forçada: obrigar as notas a se encaixarem numa curva fixa.

items.q: "An appraisal that only scores last year's results is backward-looking." This means it…
options: is reviewed by an external auditor
focuses on what has already happened rather than what comes next
items.why: Backward-looking = retrospectivo: olha para o que já passou, não para o que vem à frente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Pay is set in a twice-yearly ___ session, where leaders compare ratings across teams for fairness."
items.why: Calibration = calibragem: reunião em que se comparam avaliações entre times para garantir consistência.

items.q: "Boiling a whole year of work down to a single number feels reductive." Reductive means…
items.why: Reductive = redutor: simplifica demais, apagando a nuance que importa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de redesenho de RH. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new appraisal model." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the monthly check-ins division by division." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Several senior managers pushed back on dropping the ratings." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team promised honest feedback but never followed through." They…
options: failed to do what they had committed to
carried it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, o que faltou.

items.q: "Renaming the form won't move the needle on engagement." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.
